body:
For my downstream applications it is really useful to just be able to go with the default opset version, but for logging purposes and model versioning it would still be nice to know the opset version that was used. Currently the `ONNX_DEFAULT_OPSET` is in the private module `torch/onnx/_constants.py`, which is why I am hesitant to use the constant directly. Would it be possible to make this a public constant? It has been there for multiple years, so I would consider it stable.

cc @justinchuby @titaiwangms

comments.body: Can you read the opset version from the onnx file? In the end that’s what matters.

I can @justinchuby, and I guess I can use that to create a workaround. For my use case however, it would be more convenient to directly have access to the opset: I am trying to cache exported models, and in order to check whether the model file has to be recreated or not, I save the file together with a hashed footprint of a couple of relevant parameters like torch version, onnx version etc. – optimally the opset would be in there as well.
If you can't make it public, I'll probably just resort to always defining the opset (probably the minimum one that works with that specific model).
Yes, explicit is recommended, as the default will change with the PyTorch version. We recommend opset 18+. (20 or 21 is the default I think. <=17 is unsupported)

title: Make `ONNX_DEFAULT_OPSET` public.
